subject: [bsp][stm32] fix variable init
label: already_ok
evidence: The two hunks move the GPIO_InitStruct declaration in stm32_pin_irq_enable to the top of the enable branch and give it a zero initializer (commit message: "fix variable init"); before the fix the struct had no initializer and only Pin, Speed, Pull and Mode were assigned before HAL_GPIO_Init, so every other member, and Pull/Mode when the mode matched no case, was stack garbage. The hk32 copy, hk32_pin_irq_enable, also declares GPIO_InitStruct without an initializer, but in the enable branch it calls GPIO_StructInit(&GPIO_InitStruct) and EXTI_StructInit(&EXTI_InitStruct) before assigning any field and before GPIO_Init/EXTI_Init. In the HK32 standard peripheral library in the same repository, GPIO_StructInit assigns all five members of GPIO_InitTypeDef (GPIO_Pin, GPIO_Mode, GPIO_Speed, GPIO_OType, GPIO_PuPd), so no member reaches GPIO_Init uninitialized, including the rising-and-falling case that sets no pull. Outside the scope of this pair: in the disable branch of the same hk32 function, NVIC_InitStruct.NVIC_IRQChannel is assigned only when no other pin of the IRQ group is still enabled, yet NVIC_Init is called unconditionally; that is a different uninitialized-variable issue with no counterpart in the stm32 fix.

subject: [BSP] add bsp for st's new platform stm32h7s7-st-disco.   [drv] STM32H7RSxx_HAL bsp fixed and update.   [add] bsp stm32h7s7-dk README.md
label: not_a_fix
evidence: All four hunks extend the stm32 GPIO driver to the STM32H7RS series that this commit adds (commit message: "add bsp for st's new platform stm32h7s7-st-disco" and "STM32H7RSxx_HAL bsp fixed and update"): they add SOC_SERIES_STM32H7RS to the conditions that select one EXTI interrupt per line and the per-line EXTI handlers, add __STM32_PORT_MAX entries for GPIOM to GPIOP (moving GPIOZ to 16), and enable the GPIOM to GPIOP clocks when the HAL defines those macros. None of these lines corrects the behaviour of a series the driver already supported; they are new chip support, so the listed hunks are not a bug fix. The ft32 copy would not need them anyway: its pin_irq_map, EXTI handlers and clock setup are selected only by SOC_SERIES_FT32F0 and SOC_SERIES_FT32F4 (the only series in bsp/ft32/libraries/Kconfig), its port table stops at GPIOF, and rt_hw_pin_init enables a fixed list of GPIO clocks through RCC_AHBPeriphClockCmd / RCC_AHB1PeriphClockCmd rather than __HAL_RCC_GPIOx_CLK_ENABLE.

None of these lines corrects the behaviour of a series the driver already supported; they are new chip support, so the listed hunks are not a bug fix. The hk32 copy would not need them anyway: the only series in bsp/hk32/libraries/Kconfig is SOC_SERIES_HK32F0XX, its pin_irq_map and EXTI handlers are hard-wired to the EXTI0_1 / EXTI2_3 / EXTI4_15 grouping with no series conditions, and the HK32F0xx device headers define only GPIOA to GPIOD and GPIOF, so the GPIOM to GPIOP entries and clocks have nothing to refer to. Its port table still starts at GPIOZ = 12 like the pre-commit stm32 table, which is harmless because no HK32 header defines GPIOZ.

subject: bsp: fm33lc026: Fix GPIO IRQ map lookup
label: already_ok
evidence: The listed hunks fix fm33lc026's range-based lookup: pin2irqindex walks a pin_irq_map whose entries hold the highest encoded pin number of each 4-pin EXTI group, and the fix stops the loop from reading one entry past the end ("<= ITEM_NUM" became "< ITEM_NUM") and from reading entry -1 at index 0, and makes fm33_pin_dettach_irq and the disable branch of fm33_pin_irq_enable pass the encoded pin instead of the PIN_STPIN bit mask, which that range search cannot match (commit message: "Keep pin2irqindex within the pin_irq_map bounds ... Pass encoded pin values to the IRQ map lookup path"). The ft32 copy has no pin2irqindex and no range-encoded map: its struct pin_irq_map holds a pinbit, the table has one entry per pin bit, and the index comes from bit2bitno, which returns the bit position or -1 and is always followed by an explicit "< 0 || >= ITEM_NUM(pin_irq_map)" check, so there is no read past the end and no read of entry -1. Its detach path (bit2bitno(PIN_FTPIN(pin))) and disable path (get_pin_irq_map(PIN_FTPIN(pin))) pass the bit mask on purpose, because bit2bitno and get_pin_irq_map(uint32_t pinbit) take a bit mask, and attach and enable compute the index from the same PIN_FTPIN(pin) key, so all four paths agree. Hunk 2 therefore has no counterpart on the ft32 side, and hunks 1 and 3 correspond to ft32 code written so that the key mismatch never existed.

subject: [bsp][n32] n32hxxx: bound the XSPI waits and fix I2C/SPI/NAND edge cases
label: not_needed_absent
evidence: The four listed hunks fix the n32hxxx SPI DMA path: spixfer scales each DMA chunk's buffer offset by the data width because already_send_length counts elements, n32_spi_lli_build advances each linked-list node's memory address by SPI_DMA_BLOCK_MAX elements times the transfer width instead of SPI_DMA_BLOCK_MAX bytes, and SPI_DMA_Transmit / SPI_DMA_Receive now return -RT_ERROR when n32_spi_dma_arm fails (commit message: "the H7xx LLI chain advanced the memory side by SPI_DMA_BLOCK_MAX bytes although BlkTfrSize counts elements" and "Propagate the DMA arm failure that was ignored"). The tm4c123 copy has none of this code: its whole transfer is a polled loop in spixfer that pushes message->length frames through SSIDataPut / SSIBusy / SSIDataGet in a single pass, with no DMA, no chunking (no already_send_length or chunk offset), no linked-list descriptors and no DMA-arm call whose result could be dropped. The BSP_SPIx_TX/RX_USING_DMA options in the tm4c123 board Kconfig are not referenced anywhere in drv_spi.c, and struct tm4c123_spi_config holds only the SSI base address and the bus name, so there is no DMA channel to set up. Separately, the polled loop indexes both buffers one byte per frame with no data-width scaling; that is a different matter from the DMA chunk and LLI offsets these hunks fix.

subject: [nxp][mcx] add frdm-mcxa366 support (#11243)
label: not_a_fix
evidence: The commit message is "[nxp][mcx] add frdm-mcxa366 support", and the listed hunks only add a new macro MCXA_UART_USE_FRO_LF_DIV that extends the existing MCXA346 CPU list with the new MCXA366 part numbers, then use that macro in place of the old MCXA346-only condition when choosing kFRO_LF_DIV_to_LPUARTx versus kFRO12M_to_LPUARTx. For every CPU supported before the commit the selected clock is unchanged, so the hunks enable a newly added chip rather than correct wrong behaviour. The other side (the MCXE driver, used only by frdm-mcxe247) would not need it anyway: its struct mcx_uart has no clock_attach_id member and no CPU_MCXA conditions, and it selects the UART clock with CLOCK_SetIpSrc using kCLOCK_IpSrcSysOscAsync.

label: not_a_fix
evidence: The commit message is "[BSP] add bsp for st's new platform stm32h7s7-st-disco. [drv] STM32H7RSxx_HAL bsp fixed and update.", and every listed hunk enables that newly added STM32H7RS series: three drv_usart.c hunks add SOC_SERIES_STM32H7RS to the lists that pick TDR/RDR over DR, and the drv_gpio.c hunks add H7RS to the per-line EXTI IRQ map and handlers and add GPIO ports M to P (port count and clock enables). None of them corrects behaviour on a series that was already supported, so this is new-platform support, not a bug fix. The other side is a separate driver for the Nations N32H7xx/N32H49x/N32H47x_48x series and has nothing to attach these hunks to: its port count __N32_PORT_MAX is keyed on SOC_SERIES_N32 macros, GPIO clocks are enabled through RCC_EnableAHB5PeriphClk2/RCC_EnableAHB1PeriphClk, and n32_putc/n32_getc use USART_SendData/USART_ReceiveData with no SOC_SERIES_STM32 conditions or TDR/RDR selection anywhere in either file.

subject: [stm32][pandora] fix LCD init ahead PWM
label: already_ok
evidence: The fix ("[stm32][pandora] fix LCD init ahead PWM") moves Pandora's rt_hw_lcd_init, which turns on the backlight through rt_device_find("pwm4"), from INIT_DEVICE_EXPORT to INIT_COMPONENT_EXPORT, so it runs after stm32_pwm_init, which the shared STM32 PWM driver registers with INIT_DEVICE_EXPORT; at the same level the LCD init could run before the PWM device exists. The rt-spark LCD driver has no rt_hw_lcd_init; its hardware bring-up function drv_lcd_init, which calls LCD_PWM_BackLightInit (rt_device_find(PWM_BL_NAME)) and LCD_BackLightSet(80) when BSP_USING_ONBOARD_LCD_PWM_BL is set, is already registered with INIT_COMPONENT_EXPORT. Its only device-level function, drv_lcd_hw_init, just fills in and registers the "lcd" device and does not touch PWM. So the rt-spark side already runs its PWM-dependent LCD init after the PWM devices are registered, which is the ordering the fix establishes.

subject: [bsp][stm32][rsoc]串口超时判断逻辑有问题
label: not_needed_absent
evidence: The commit message says (translated) "the UART timeout check logic has a problem" and "fix uart bug"; the hunk changes the wait loop in stm32_putc from block_timeout-- to --block_timeout, because with post-decrement the rt_uint32_t counter wraps past zero when the wait expires, so the following (block_timeout != 0) check reports success instead of -1. This is a real fix, but it lives entirely in the transmit-timeout counter. The other side's matching function ch32_putc has no such counter: it spins on USART_FLAG_TC without any limit, writes DATAR and always returns 1, struct ch32_uart has no tx_block_timeout member, and the word timeout does not occur anywhere in drv_usart_v2.c. With no timeout counter or timeout result check, the wrap-around the fix removes cannot happen there.

subject: [bsp][stm32]fix stm32h7 spi transmit fail probelm.
label: not_needed_hw
evidence: The commit "[bsp][stm32]fix stm32h7 spi transmit fail probelm." changes Init.FifoThreshold from SPI_FIFO_THRESHOLD_08DATA to SPI_FIFO_THRESHOLD_01DATA inside the STM32H7-only branch of stm32_spi_init (now shared with MP1 and N6), i.e. it retunes the configurable FIFO threshold of that chip family's SPI peripheral. The other side is the TI TM4C123 driver, which configures its SSI through TivaWare (SSIConfigSetExpClk with protocol, mode, bit rate and data width, then SSIEnable) and moves one frame at a time with SSIDataPut, SSIBusy and SSIDataGet; it has no FIFO threshold setting and no SOC_SERIES_STM32H7 branch. The repository's TivaWare register map for the TM4C123 SSI lists only CR0, CR1, DR, SR, CPSR, IM, RIS, MIS, ICR, DMACTL, PP and CC, and ssi.h describes the FIFO interrupt levels as fixed ("TX FIFO half full or less", "RX FIFO half full or more"). So the configurable FIFO threshold the fix depends on does not exist on that chip.
